title: Introduce cumulative utilization prober and anticipatory scale smoother
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: we observe recurring short-lived oscillations in Dedicated fleet scaling where bursts followed by rapid drains produce noisy utilization signals. Existing percentile-based samplers underweight cumulative idle capacity and therefore trigger unnecessary scale-ups that later compete with corrections, increasing churn and tail latency. This PR adds a lightweight probing/telemetry component that measures cumulative available capacity across configurable windows and an anticipatory smoothing layer in the autoscaler that uses that signal to dampen reactive scale-ups.
detailed_body: This PR implements two coordinated features as a single user-facing capability (feature-flag gated): 1) cumulative-utilization-prober: a periodic probe that aggregates per-pool occupancy and idle-slot duration into a single timeseries (redwood.fleet.cum_idle_seconds and redwood.fleet.cum_utilization_ratio) reported at 10s and 2m rollups; it also computes an outlier-resistant decay-adjusted headroom estimate (redwood.fleet.decayed_headroom_est) for downstream decisioning. 2) anticipatory-scale-smoother: an autoscaler stage that ingests decayed_headroom_est and applies a predictive damping coefficient to scale decisions — effectively increasing the confidence threshold for scale-up actions when cumulative headroom suggests transient drain. The smoother operates as a multiplicative governor applied after the baseline scale decision and before any commitment/reservation steps. Rationale: the cumulative probe captures multi-second/multi-minute persistence of excess capacity which percentile samplers may miss, and the smoother prevents rapid oscillation between scaling states while preserving the ability to satisfy sustained demand.

review_comments:
Evan: requested clarification on edge cases when decayed_headroom is noisy during multi-region failover; suggested bounding damping coefficient to [0.5,1.0].
Aisha: added unit tests and clamped coefficients; updated docs to explain multi-region behavior.
Priya: asked for telemetry naming consistency with existing percentile metrics; changed metric prefixes and updated dashboards.
Liam: approved after CI flake was resolved and an extra integration test was added to the sim harness.
ci_checks: CI summary: build (pass), unit tests (pass), integration (pass), linters (pass), e2e sim (pass). Note: an earlier integration job failed due to race in the sim harness; fixed by introducing deterministic clocks in tests and re-running.
deployment_notes: Feature is behind 'anticipatory_smoother' flag. Default off for 2 weeks in prod. Canary rollout plan: enable on 5% of Dedicated pools in us-west1 for 48h, monitor redwood.fleet.cum_utilization_ratio and tail L95 latency, then expand to 25% then 100% if stable. If cumulative_headroom drops unexpectedly or tail latency regresses >5% relative, rollback by toggling the flag. Operator docs updated with flag and tuning knobs: probe_window_seconds, decay_half_life_seconds, damping_min, damping_max.
observability_and_alerting: Added dashboard 'Fleet Cumulative Headroom' and two alerts: 1) Alert if decayed_headroom_est < -0.1 for 5m across >10% of pools (possible sustained underprovisioning), 2) Alert if smoothing_coefficient frequently toggles above 0.95 causing suppressed scale-ups. Both alerts include runbook steps to flip feature flag and inspect sim logs.
release_notes: Added a telemetry-driven autoscaler smoother to reduce oscillatory scale events by considering cumulative idle capacity across short and medium windows; feature is opt-in behind a feature flag and will be canaried.
post_merge_actions:
- cherry-pick into release/2025-04-critical-fixes for a quick canary deployment
- coordinate with SRE on canary timeline (scheduled 2025-04-14)
- monitor metrics for 72h and publish summary to ENG-2145 thread
notes_on_compatibility: No breaking API changes; autoscaler config adds optional fields with sane defaults. Backwards compatible with existing reservation and burst token systems. Smoother only modifies the in-memory decision pipeline and is reversible via the feature flag.
testing_summary: Unit coverage: +18%. Integration tests simulate burst->drain patterns with and without smoother; result: 32% reduction in churned scale events in sim and 8-12% reduction in 95th token latency in controlled perf lab runs.
